text: SHOCKING! Doctors hate this secret: one cup of guava leaf tea cures diabetes in 3 days. Share before they delete this!
Fake: a secret cure, "doctors hate it" and a rush to share are classic tricks.
Barangay Health Desk
The DOH reminds everyone to wash hands with soap and water. Visit your nearest health center for free vaccines for children.
Real: calm, practical advice that points to your health center.
Bilis Gumaling Shop
100% guaranteed miracle pill melts fat and cures cancer. No doctor needed. Order now, only 50 left!
Fake: "100% guaranteed", "miracle" and "no doctor needed" are red flags.
Kalusugan Muna Page
WHO advises that adults get at least 150 minutes of moderate exercise each week. Ask your doctor what is safe for you.
Real: a well-known health guideline that tells you to ask a doctor.
Ang Totoo Daw Channel
Government is hiding the truth: vaccines contain microchips. Wake up and share with everyone you love!
Fake: a hidden-truth story with no proof and a push to share.
Tita Ana, Health Worker
If you have a fever for more than three days, see a health worker. Drink plenty of fluids and rest at home meanwhile.
Real: sensible advice that sends you to a health worker.
Lutong Lola Tips
Drink hot water with garlic every hour and the virus dies. A famous doctor says this cures everything. Forward to 10 friends!
Fake: one cure for everything and an unnamed "famous doctor".
Sagip Lamok Barangay
Dengue spreads through mosquito bites. Remove standing water around your home every week. The local health office can help.
Real: a well-established fact with a simple action.
Natural Lang Po
Secret cure for high blood pressure found. Stop taking your medicine and use this herbal powder instead. Guaranteed!
Fake: never stop your medicine because of a post. A health worker decides.
Klinika ng Bayan
Vaccines are tested for safety before use. Talk to your health worker at the barangay clinic about the schedule for your family.
Real: it explains a fact and points to your health worker.
Sun Tap
Tap, click or press Space to keep the sun glowing.
Arrow keys and swipes work too.
If the glow runs out you lose a heart. Three hearts, then the run is over.
Hello, test pilot!
This little game is only here for testing the Arcade.
The idea
Keep the sun glowing for as long as you can.
Tap, click or press Space. Swipes and arrow keys count too.
Why it matters
Real games here teach how to stay safe from health misinformation.
When the source is clear and the facts can be checked.
When should I trust it? When I can check who said it.
"Press Start 2P", ui-monospace, monospace
You are the algorithm. Pick one of 3 posts to show the person before the timer ends.
Press the left and right arrows (or A and D), then Space or Enter. You can also tap or click a post.
CLICKS shows how much attention a post is likely to win. Scary posts win the most.
Scary posts push Engagement up but shrink the Feed Bubble and drain Balanced Feed. Trusted health tips and new topics refill it.
Gold chips are what the person likes. Each person has 10 posts, then comes the next one. Finish with both meters above 50 for a bonus.
The run ends when Balanced Feed or Engagement hits 0.
Today, YOU are the algorithm!
Tita Baby is scrolling, and you choose what she sees next. No pressure. Okay, a little pressure.
Feeds pick what keeps people scrolling
An algorithm shows more of whatever gets clicks. Keep Tita interested, but keep her feed balanced.
Pick one of three posts before the timer ends. Use left and right with Enter, or just tap a post.
Scary health posts get clicks, so feeds show more of them. That can trap people in a bubble of fear.
Trust a feed that shows you many sides, and search on purpose for trusted sources.
When should I trust it? When a feed shows me many sides, and I search on purpose for trusted sources.

Barangay Masagana
DENGUE PREVENTION
a dengue-prevention poster
DOH and WHO dengue guidance: mosquitoes breed in standing water; see a health worker for a lasting fever.
No water, no mosquitoes!
Dry surroundings, safe family!
Stop the sting, empty the thing!
Empty standing water every week. Mosquitoes breed in it.
Mosquitoes lay eggs in standing water, so emptying it every week breaks the cycle.
A fever that will not go away? See a health worker early.
Early care matters in dengue, and only a health worker can tell what is wrong.
Papaya leaf juice cures dengue.
No home drink cures dengue. People with a fever should see a health worker.
Dengue spreads when people cough or sneeze.
Dengue spreads by mosquito bites, not by coughs or sneezes.
HANDWASHING WEEK
a handwashing poster
WHO and DOH hand hygiene guidance: soap, clean water and about 20 seconds, at key moments.
Soap and water, always ready!
Clean hands, healthy town!
Scrub, rinse, repeat, stay neat!
Wash hands with soap and clean water for at least 20 seconds.
Soap and about 20 seconds of scrubbing lift germs off your skin.
Wash before eating and after using the toilet.
These are the moments when germs most easily travel from hands to mouths.
Wash only if your hands look dirty.
Germs are too small to see. Wash at the key moments even when hands look clean.
Cold water cannot clean hands. Only hot water works.
Soap and scrubbing do the work. Clean cold water is fine.
VACCINATION DAY
a vaccination-day poster
DOH Expanded Program on Immunization and WHO: routine child vaccines are free at health centers and do not cause the disease.
Vaccines today, kids protected!
Bring baby, it is free at the health center!
A small shot, a big shield!
Routine childhood vaccines are free at the barangay health center.
The government immunization program gives routine vaccines for children at health centers.
Bring your child’s vaccine card so the health worker can check what is due.
The card shows which vaccines were given, so nothing is missed.
Vaccines give children the very disease they protect against.
Vaccines train the body to fight a disease. They do not cause the disease.
One shot as a baby protects against everything for life.
Different vaccines need different doses and timing. Ask the health worker.
CHECK YOUR BP
a blood-pressure check poster
DOH and WHO hypertension guidance: high blood pressure often has no signs, and too much salt raises it.
Your pressure: know it!
Free check-up, health is the prize!
Know your number, love your heart!
Get your blood pressure checked often, even when you feel fine.
High blood pressure often has no signs, so a check is the only way to know.
Too much salt can raise blood pressure over time.
